Integrate runnable leases with Waiting, resume, and restart (#189)

codeon:
  version: 1
  authority: fewensa-51
  description: |-
    # Objective
    
    Integrate the durable runnable-lease state machine into actual Attempt, Operation, Agent/runtime, Waiting, Attention, activation, and startup reconciliation paths so Waiting can free execution capacity without permitting stale or possibly-live work to continue.
    
    # Dependency and handoff
    
    Blocked by the durable runnable-lease state-machine Task. Consume its store APIs and generation fence; do not bypass them with direct SQL.
    
    This PR must finish lease lifecycle integration before the daemon-owned Observer Task begins. It may use fake/manual observation inputs for integration tests, but it does not own the production auto-observation worker.
    
    # Owned scope
    
    - pure release/resume eligibility policy;
    - runtime quiescence/reaping/not-applicable evidence binding;
    - Waiting and Execution Attention open/resolution transaction participants;
    - activation outbox and execution-runtime resume fencing;
    - scheduler ordering between ready resumptions and new claims;
    - startup reconciliation of held/released leases;
    - daemon integration tests and operational diagnostics;
    - owning normative docs/OpenWiki updates.
    
    # Release authority
    
    A runnable lease may be released only when one of these durable facts is available:
    
    1. the Agent/runtime reports terminal and independent containment/process readback proves quiescence;
    2. Codeon successfully reaps the owned process tree and independently confirms it is gone;
    3. the current Operation kind has an explicit not-applicable runtime-ownership contract;
    4. the Attempt enters a receipt-backed terminal state.
    
    The following must hold the lease:
    
    - runtime outcome unknown;
    - process/cgroup readback incomplete;
    - possibly-live child process;
    - provider or persistence ambiguity that does not prove runtime closure;
    - stale dispatch/operation authority;
    - Agent message text without structured completion and terminal evidence;
    - daemon shutdown before quiescence is proven.
    
    Recovery Required does not automatically mean released. The runtime evidence decides.
    
    # Atomic Waiting/Attention open
    
    For an owner that enters Waiting or Recovery Required after runtime closure, one owner transaction must:
    
    ```text
    lock Attempt + Operation + dispatch/runtime authority
    validate quiescence evidence
    open/update Waiting or Execution Attention
    apply RuntimeLeaseDecision
    release the runnable lease when authorized
    persist activation/resume checkpoint and next_observe_at/operator action
    commit all effects together
    ```
    
    No observable state may say Waiting with a released lease unless the same transaction committed the owner checkpoint. No lease may be released while the runtime owner remains ambiguous.
    
    # Atomic resume and activation
    
    When owner policy says an Attempt may resume:
    
    1. validate current Attention/owner/Attempt/Operation versions and latest observation digest;
    2. attempt runnable-lease reacquisition under global capacity authority;
    3. if capacity is full, persist a stable `ready_to_resume_capacity_pending` state without busy retry;
    4. if acquired, bind the new lease generation into the activation/dispatch authority;
    5. enqueue activation in the same transaction;
    6. only a worker presenting that exact generation may perform Agent start/resume or mutating provider I/O.
    
    A delayed worker with an older generation must fail before external I/O.
    
    # Resume fairness
    
    Already-active ready-to-resume Attempts must receive bounded priority over admitting new Issues:
    
    - durable ready-resume candidates ordered by ready timestamp and stable identity;
    - each scheduler/runtime tick processes a bounded number first;
    - remaining capacity may admit new Issues;
    - fairness remains scoped and deterministic;
    - no priority rule bypasses blockers, Profile authority, Repository verification, current owner evidence, or fences;
    - capacity pending is not a hot loop.
    
    Avoid a broad scheduler rewrite. Add the smallest deterministic coordination needed to prevent starvation.
    
    # Startup reconciliation
    
    Before readiness:
    
    - held + confirmed runtime active: preserve held;
    - held + confirmed quiescent with valid owner state: apply the legal release transition;
    - held + unknown runtime: preserve held and enter/reaffirm Recovery Required;
    - released + resume pending: keep released and queue bounded reacquisition;
    - released + discovered live runtime: fail closed as authority conflict;
    - terminal + held: idempotently complete terminal release;
    - missing/corrupt lease projection: stop affected execution and expose bounded recovery evidence.
    
    Do not release capacity merely to make startup succeed.
    
    # Canonical A-E integration scenario
    
    Configure total-active 8 and runnable 4.
    
    A, B, C, and D run with held leases; E cannot start. A publishes a PR and waits for checks. Codeon independently proves A's process tree quiescent. The same transaction opens A's Waiting/Attention owner checkpoint and releases A's lease. A remains active, so total-active is still consumed. E then claims the free runnable slot and starts.
    
    A later receives a checks-passed observation through a fake/manual owner path. B, C, D, and E still occupy four slots, so A becomes `ready_to_resume_capacity_pending` and no Agent starts. When B terminally releases its lease, A is the oldest ready resume, atomically reacquires generation 2, enqueues activation, and resumes Review/Revision. At no point are more than four runnable leases held, and an old generation-1 worker cannot perform I/O.
    
    Also test the unsafe variant: if A's runtime readback is unknown, A enters Recovery Required but keeps its held lease; E remains unable to start. This proves recovery cannot manufacture capacity.
    
    # Observability
    
    Expose bounded fields sufficient to diagnose:
    
    ```text
    total_active_count
    total_active_capacity
    runnable_held_count
    runnable_capacity
    runnable_resume_pending_count
    lease_release_reason
    lease_reacquire_outcome
    lease_generation
    ```
    
    Never log token material, prompts, Agent output, raw provider bodies, unbounded stdout/stderr, or worktree content.
    
    # Documentation and OpenWiki
    
    Update the lifecycle, Attention, scheduler, startup reconciliation, and capacity sections of `docs/spec/picker-runtime.md`, then run `openwiki code --update --print`. Preserve the complete A-E scenario in the owning architecture context. The final Observer Task will consolidate the final three-pool explanation in OpenWiki. Do not add a standalone plan/report.
    
    # Non-goals
    
    - No production automatic Observer loop.
    - No new provider request limiter.
    - No changing Issue workflow semantics.
    - No automatic force-success or recovery bypass.
    - No production capacity value change.
    - No broad execution-runtime rewrite unrelated to lease fencing.
    - No cleanup of unrelated legacy states.
    
    # Verification
    
    Cover:
    
    - all release-authority classifications;
    - atomic Waiting open plus release;
    - transaction rollback leaves both owner and lease unchanged;
    - capacity-pending resume;
    - reacquire plus activation atomicity;
    - stale generation refusal before external I/O;
    - resume priority and bounded fairness;
    - unknown runtime retains held capacity;
    - shutdown at each boundary;
    - startup reconciliation matrix;
    - daemon crash before/after commit;
    - A-E safe and unsafe variants;
    - fake Agent/runtime integration proving process concurrency never exceeds runnable capacity.
    
    Run focused domain, PostgreSQL, daemon integration, format, clippy, migration acceptance inherited from the blocker, and repository verification.
    
    # Definition of done
    
    Waiting genuinely frees runnable capacity only when runtime closure is proven; resumption cannot execute without a current lease generation; restart preserves the same authority; and the A-E scenario works end-to-end without a production Observer loop.
    
    ---
    
    # Post-creation review enrichment
    
    ## Exact orchestration
    
    - Parent: `fewensa-49`.
    - Blocked by: `fewensa-53`.
    - Blocks: `fewensa-52`.
    - Do not start until `fewensa-53` is receipt-finalized and merged.
    - Update local main and use only the merged store API; direct runnable-lease SQL is forbidden.
    
    ## Corrected runtime boundary
    
    A runnable lease is required before starting, resuming, steering, or otherwise granting execution authority to an Agent/runtime. It is not automatically required for every Codeon-owned SCM provider operation.
    
    For Publication, Merge, RejectClose, cleanup, or another non-Agent phase:
    
    - derive runtime ownership from the typed phase contract;
    - when runtime is not applicable, release/classify the lease only through durable evidence;
    - continue to fence SCM mutations with the phase's existing intent/checkpoint/readback/outcome-unknown contract;
    - reacquire only when the next selected phase needs Agent/runtime capacity.
    
    The A-E scenario specifically resumes an Agent-backed Review/Revision phase, so A must reacquire there.
    
    ## Transaction ownership rule
    
    Do not introduce a cross-store pseudo-transaction assembled in daemon code. Extend the existing owner transaction-participant boundary so Attention/Waiting, lease release/reacquire, and activation outbox effects share one real PostgreSQL transaction.
    
    ## Fairness and safety gate
    
    Ready resumptions receive bounded priority, not unconditional starvation of new claims. Tests must cover multiple Profiles and repositories, persistent capacity pending without busy polling, and unknown runtime evidence retaining a held lease.
    
    Review must reject any path that releases solely because Attempt state is Waiting or RecoveryRequired.
